lyrics:
[Intro: plucked strings, soft kick, a little synth sparkle]

[Verse 1: bright, breathy, light beat]
I had a list for today
Milk and stamps and a key
Then you held the door at the bank
Now I can't remember three

[Pre-Chorus: beat builds, voice quickens]
I don't do this, I plan things
I've got a calendar with tabs
But something about a Tuesday
Has me skipping all the steps

[Chorus: full beat, string stabs after every line]
No pressure, but
I've already named the dog
No pressure, but
I told my mother and my blog
It's only been an hour
I know it's early days
No pressure, but
I've cleared my Saturdays

[Verse 2: bright, laughing]
You said your name, I think
I was looking at your hands
You asked me for the time
And I gave you all my plans

[Pre-Chorus: beat builds, voice quickens]
I don't do this, I plan things
I colour-code my shoes
But something about your raincoat
Has me giving up the rules

[Chorus: full beat, string stabs after every line]
No pressure, but
I've already named the dog
No pressure, but
I told my mother and my blog
It's only been an hour
I know it's early days
No pressure, but
I've cleared my Saturdays

[Bridge: beat drops to claps, voice close]
I didn't know that I was waiting
Until the waiting stopped
I didn't know that I was waiting
And now I can't find the clock

[Final Chorus: everything, extra strings, gang vocals on the hedge]
No pressure, but
I've already named the dog
No pressure, but
I told my mother and my blog
It's only been an hour
I know it's early days
No pressure, but
I've cleared my Saturdays

[Outro: string stab, spoken, a giggle]
No pressure
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 120 BPM, 4/4, G major. A bright, bouncing, four-on-the-floor pop pulse. Sunny and slightly out of breath.

VOICE: Female soprano, sweet, light and a little breathy, with a girlish brightness that suits the joke. Quick and chatty in the verses. The chorus is clear and punchy, with a group of friends joining on the repeated title phrase in the last chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A synthesised string section playing short, bright stabs after each chorus line, plus plucked strings in the verses. A steady kick on every beat with handclaps. Clean, chiming electric guitar. A bouncing synth bass. Sparkling synth arpeggios. Tambourine.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, plucked strings. 0:08 Verse 1. 0:24 Pre-chorus. 0:40 Chorus 1 with string stabs. 1:12 Verse 2. 1:28 Pre-chorus. 1:44 Chorus 2. 2:16 Bridge, the beat drops to claps. 2:32 Final chorus with extra strings and gang vocals. 3:04 Outro, one last stab, two spoken words and a giggle at 3:12.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2010s bubblegum pop: bright, clean and compressed, strings and vocal very forward, a tight punchy low end.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first string stab after the first chorus line at 0:42.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: She is a grown woman with a tabbed calendar, and the joke is that she skips the coy stage entirely. The bridge's impossible line is about someone who did not know she was lonely until it stopped.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Fluster, comic overreach, one sincere moment, delight.
